welcome.title: Let's connect your Gmail accounts
welcome.lead: This setup takes about 15 minutes and you do it only once. After that, AI apps like Claude can read, sort and draft mail in every Gmail account you connect.
welcome.plan1: Create a free Google Cloud project. It gives you your own private key to Gmail.
welcome.plan2: Upload that key file to this page.
welcome.plan3: Sign in to each Gmail account you want to use, and give it a name you like.
welcome.plan4: Add multiple-gmail to your AI app.
welcome.privacy: Your sign-ins are stored encrypted on this computer only. multiple-gmail has no server of its own and nobody else sees your mail.
welcome.keepOpen: Keep the multiple-gmail window (the black window that opened with this page) open while you work here. Closing it stops this page.
welcome.keepOpen_mac: Keep the Terminal window that opened with this page open while you work here. Closing it stops this page.
welcome.keepOpen_linux: Keep the terminal window where multiple-gmail is running open while you work here. Closing it stops this page.

google.title: Set up Google Cloud
google.lead: Google needs to know that multiple-gmail may use Gmail for you. You tell it in Google Cloud, Google's website for app settings. It is free: you do not need billing or a credit card.
google.open: Open this page in Google Cloud

s1.title: Create a project
s1.why: A project is a folder in Google Cloud that keeps your settings together.
s1.do1: Sign in with any Google account. Your personal Gmail is fine.
s1.do2: Type a project name, for example multiple-gmail, and click Create.
s1.do3: Wait a few seconds. Check that the new project is selected in the project picker at the top of the page.

s2.title: Turn on the Gmail API
s2.why: The Gmail API is the door that lets a program like multiple-gmail work with Gmail.
s2.do1: Check that your new project is selected at the top of the page.

s3.title: Describe your app
s3.why: Google shows this on its sign-in screen. Only you will see it.
s3.do1: Open Google Auth Platform and click Get started.
s3.do2: App information: type an app name, for example My Gmail helper, and choose your email as the user support email. Click Next.
s3.do4: Contact information: type your email. Click Next.
s3.do5: Tick the box to agree to the Google API Services User Data Policy, then click Continue and Create.
s3.do6: Open Branding. Under App domain, fill in Application home page, Application privacy policy link and Authorized domains, then click Save. If you have no website of your own, use this project's public pages: home page https://efk44.github.io/multiple-gmail/ , privacy policy https://efk44.github.io/multiple-gmail/privacy.html , authorized domain efk44.github.io . If you have your own domain, you may use that instead. Publishing in the last step stays disabled until these are filled in.

s4.title: Allow Gmail access
s4.why: A scope is a permission. This one lets multiple-gmail read, label, draft and send mail. It cannot delete mail for good.
s4.do1: Open Data access and click Add or remove scopes.
s4.do2: At the bottom of the panel, find Manually add scopes. Paste the address below and click Add to table.
s4.do3: Click Update, then click Save at the bottom of the page.

s5.title: Create the key file
s5.why: The client is your app's ID card. Google gives it to you as a small file with a name like client_secret_123.json.
s5.do1: Open Clients and click Create client.
s5.do2: Application type: choose Desktop app. Name: anything, for example multiple-gmail desktop.
s5.do3: Tick the box "Use this client for an AI-powered agent" if you see it, then click Create.
s5.note: Download it right away. Google may show the secret part only once. If you missed it, delete the client and create a new one.
s5.do4: In the window that opens, click Download JSON and save the file where you can find it, for example in Downloads.

s6.title: Publish the app
s6.why: New apps start in Testing mode. In Testing mode Google signs you out every 7 days and you would have to reconnect every account each week. Publishing stops that.
s6.do1: Open Audience. Under Publishing status, click Publish app, then Confirm.
s6.do2: If Publish app is greyed out, hover over it to see what is missing. It is almost always the App domain fields on the Branding page (see the earlier step).
s6.do3: The status should now say In production.
s6.do4: Google may say your app needs verification. You can ignore that: verification is for apps that other people use.
s6.do5: Prefer not to publish? You can stay in Testing: open Audience, add each Gmail address under Test users. Tokens then expire every 7 days and multiple-gmail shows Reconnect next to the account.

google.aheadTitle: Two screens you will see when you sign in later
google.ahead1: This is expected. The app is yours: you made it a few minutes ago and only your own accounts use it. Click Advanced, then click Go to (your app name) (unsafe).
google.ahead2: Next, Google lists what the app may do. If the box next to the Gmail permission (read, compose and send email) is empty, tick it. Without it multiple-gmail cannot see your mail.

upload.title: Upload the key file
upload.lead: Choose the JSON file you downloaded from Google Cloud. Its name usually starts with client_secret and ends with .json.
upload.ok: Key file saved. multiple-gmail keeps it encrypted on this computer.
upload.already: A key file is already saved. Uploading a new one replaces it.
upload.webWarning: This file belongs to a Web application client. multiple-gmail needs a Desktop app client. Go back to the Google Cloud guide, step 5, and create a Desktop app client.
upload.clientChanged: This key file belongs to a different Google client than the one your accounts were connected with. Click Reconnect on every account to sign in again.
upload.secret: This file contains a secret. Do not share it or send it to anyone.

err.tooBig: This file is too big to be a key file. Choose the client_secret JSON file.
err.notJson: This is not a JSON file. Download the client JSON again from Google Cloud (Clients, then Download JSON).
err.serviceAccount: This is a service account key, not the file we need. In Google Cloud go to Clients and create a client of type Desktop app.
err.notClient: This JSON file is not a Google client file. Download the JSON from Google Cloud, Clients, Desktop app.
err.missingId: The file is missing the client ID. Download it again from Google Cloud.
err.missingSecret: The file is missing the client secret. Google shows the secret only once: delete the client, create a new Desktop app client and download its JSON right away.

accounts.title: Connect your Gmail accounts
accounts.lead: Give each account a name you like. You will use it with your AI, for example: show me the newest mail in Work.
accounts.nameHint: Any name you like, up to 40 characters, e.g. "Kişisel", "İş Hesabı", "Work".
accounts.emailHint: If you type it, Google picks this account for you on the sign-in page.
accounts.waiting: A Google sign-in tab opened. Finish signing in there, then come back to this tab. This page updates by itself.
accounts.popupBlocked: If no new tab opened, use this link:
accounts.gaveUp: No answer from Google after 6 minutes, so this page stopped waiting. Click Connect with Google to try again.
accounts.empty: No accounts yet. Add your first one above.
accounts.more: You can add as many accounts as you like, one at a time.

nameErr.empty: Type a name for this account.
nameErr.invalid: Use letters, numbers, spaces and punctuation only.
nameErr.taken: You already have an account with this name.
nameErr.email: This is the email of a connected account. Choose another name.

failed.user_denied: Sign-in was cancelled or permission was not given. Try again, and on Google's permission screen tick the Gmail box.
failed.timeout: Sign-in took too long and was stopped. Click Connect with Google to try again.
failed.admin_blocked: Your Google Workspace administrator blocked this app. If you are the admin, follow the steps below, then try again.
failed.unknown: Google sign-in did not finish. Try again.

workspace.title: Workspace account? Do this first (optional)
workspace.lead: Only for addresses on your own company domain (Google Workspace), and only if you are its admin. Normal @gmail.com accounts skip this.
workspace.s1: Open the Google Admin console and sign in as the admin.
workspace.s2: Go to Security, then Access and data control, then API controls.
workspace.s4: Click Configure new app, choose to search by client ID, and paste your client ID.
workspace.s5: Select the app, choose who it applies to, set access to Trusted, and click Finish.
workspace.s6: Wait a few minutes, then connect the account again.
workspace.noClient: Upload the key file first to see your client ID here.

ai.title: Connect your AI app
ai.lead: Pick the app you use. You can connect more than one. Each app then sees all your Gmail accounts by their names.
ai.outdated: Added, but for a multiple-gmail file at another location. Click Update to point it at this copy.
ai.unsupported_mac: This is not available on this system.
ai.unsupported_linux: This is not available on this system.

claudeDesktop.title: Claude Desktop
claudeDesktop.desc: The Claude app for your computer. One click adds multiple-gmail to it. A backup of its settings is made first.
claudeDesktop.noticeTitle: One more step: restart Claude Desktop
claudeDesktop.notice: Now fully quit Claude Desktop: right-click the Claude icon near the clock (system tray) and choose Quit. Then open Claude Desktop again.
claudeDesktop.notice_mac: Now fully quit Claude Desktop: in the menu bar choose Claude > Quit Claude (or press Cmd+Q). Then open Claude Desktop again.
claudeDesktop.notice_linux: Now fully quit Claude Desktop, including any icon it keeps in the panel. Then open Claude Desktop again.

claudeCode.title: Claude Code
claudeCode.desc: Claude in the terminal. Run this command once in a terminal window (Command Prompt or PowerShell).
claudeCode.desc_mac: Claude in the terminal. Run this command once in a terminal window (Terminal app).
claudeCode.desc_linux: Claude in the terminal. Run this command once in a terminal window.
claudeCode.runOk: Done. Claude Code now knows multiple-gmail. Restart Claude Code to use it.
claudeCode.runFail: The command did not work (exit code {code}). Copy it and run it in a terminal to see why.
claudeCode.notFound: Claude Code was not found on this computer. If you install it later, copy the command above.

gemini.title: Gemini CLI
gemini.desc: Gemini in the terminal. This is also the way to use Gemini with your mail. One click adds multiple-gmail to its settings. A backup is made first.
gemini.done: Added to Gemini CLI. Close and reopen Gemini CLI to use it.

http.title: Other apps: Cursor, VS Code, LM Studio and more
http.desc: These apps connect to a local web address with a secret key. The multiple-gmail window must be open for them to work.
http.showKey: Show the key in the examples
http.keyHidden: The examples show <YOUR_API_KEY> until you click Show. Copy buttons always copy the real key.
http.keyWarn: Keep this key private. Anyone who has it can use your Gmail through this computer.
http.tip: Tip: turn on Start with Windows in the control panel, so these apps always find multiple-gmail.
http.tip_mac: Tip: turn on Start at login in the control panel, so these apps always find multiple-gmail.
http.tip_linux: Tip: turn on Start at login in the control panel, so these apps always find multiple-gmail.

web.title: ChatGPT and claude.ai in the browser
web.desc: Websites cannot reach a program on your computer. To use them, multiple-gmail has to run on a server in server mode. The file DEPLOY.md in the project explains how.

dashboard.title: Control panel
dashboard.lead: Setup is done. Open multiple-gmail any time to come back here.
dashboard.reconnectHint: An account that needs reconnect stopped working, usually because its Google sign-in expired. Click Reconnect and sign in again.
dashboard.apikeyDesc: Used by Cursor, VS Code and other apps that connect to the local address.
dashboard.rotateBody: The old key stops working right away. Apps that use it, like Cursor or VS Code, need the new key.
dashboard.rotated: New key made. Paste it into your other apps.
dashboard.autostartDesc: Starts multiple-gmail quietly when you sign in to Windows, so apps like Cursor can always reach it. Claude Desktop and Gemini CLI do not need this.
dashboard.autostartDesc_mac: Starts multiple-gmail quietly the next time you log in to your Mac, so apps like Cursor can always reach it. Claude Desktop and Gemini CLI do not need this.
dashboard.autostartDesc_linux: Starts multiple-gmail quietly the next time you log in to your desktop, so apps like Cursor can always reach it. Claude Desktop and Gemini CLI do not need this.
dashboard.aiDesc: Add multiple-gmail to Claude, Gemini CLI or other apps.

remove.title: Remove {name}?
remove.body: multiple-gmail signs out of this account and forgets it. Your mail in Gmail stays as it is.
remove.notRevoked: {name} was removed from this computer, but Google could not be told. You can also remove access at myaccount.google.com/permissions.

rename.title: Rename {name}
rename.body: Only the name changes. The account stays connected and your AI apps keep working.
rename.label: New name
